evidenceBasis: Completed bounded official-source review of historical production, with consolidation resolutions; not actual older-cluster integration.
currentSourceApplicability: Requires reassessment after production layout changes.

findings.change: Reintroduced admissionregistration/v1beta1 removed again; auth/v1alpha1 and VAP/v1alpha1 removed upstream
findings.assessment: OpenShift4.20 removal table includes webhook/policy configuration objects in admissionregistration/v1beta1. Upstream1.33 removes inactive authentication/v1alpha1 and VAP/v1alpha1 serving. Neither converter nor fixture inventory creates those versions. Stable workload and review endpoints retain contracts; unknown/denied discovery remains an error.
findings.validationOrRequiredAction: Continue explicit GVR versions and JSON endpoint contracts, not generic kubectl-skew claims.

findings.assessment: Feature enabled by default does not mean every Pod uses isolated user namespaces: the linked guide says hostUsers defaults true, isolated false requires suitable SCC and UID/GID range<=65535. hostUsers/procMount are baseline fields and are retained. The tool does not read/validate a whole SCC schema; it evaluates actual SA SCC-review defaulted Pod and raw Pod admission, with separate required-SCC authorization. ID-mapped mount support remains filesystem/vendor dependent (notably NFS). v2 hostmount grant is optional test setup, not ordinary converter RBAC.
findings.validationOrRequiredAction: Verify actual SA permissions/defaults, preserve hostUsers/procMount; inspect supported ID-mapped storage and namespace ranges. nested-container UID fix in4.20.35 is current policy validation, not grounds to rewrite SCCs.

findings.change: Namespace fsGroupChangePolicy/seLinuxChangePolicy defaults; RWO/RWX SELinux mount remains TP/default recursive
findings.assessment: Namespace storage.openshift.io/fsgroup-change-policy injects baseline fsGroupChangePolicy (Always/OnRootMismatch) and is retained by raw-to-typed processing. Namespace storage.openshift.io/selinux-change-policy=Recursive injects post-floor seLinuxChangePolicy and is refused for manual review. RWOP optimized mount is driver-dependent/default; RWO/RWX still recursive bydefault in these notes; do not incorrectly assert all 4.20 volumes switched mount defaults.
findings.validationOrRequiredAction: Keep raw admission-field refusal tests. Mount/relabel conflict/startup latency remains storage/runtime prerequisite; do not mutate namespace settings to bypass it.

findings.change: In-place resize beta; Pod-level hugepages and status.resize replaced by conditions
findings.assessment: The converter neither initiates Pod resize nor relies on deprecated status.resize. Container requests/status allocatedResources/status.resources maxima are counted, and observed raw Pod-level CPU/memory/hugepages requests replace corresponding container totals plus overhead. Target Pod-level budgets and native sidecars remain manual baseline features; existing other-Pod sidecars are accounted. Upstream helper comparison finds no new undercount in the assessed path.
findings.validationOrRequiredAction: Existing observed-allocation/sidecar/budget contracts must pass after dependency updates. This is a source comparison, not an old-server resize integration.

findings.change: HPA tolerance, supplementalGroupsPolicy Strict node rejection, recursiveReadOnly GA, image volumes and native sidecar GA
findings.assessment: New HPA behavior.tolerance, Pod security supplementalGroupsPolicy, VolumeMount.recursiveReadOnly, image-volume source and native sidecar restartPolicy are post-baseline fields. They require manual conversion/admission review rather than being dropped by typed clients. Strict supplemental groups can fail on unsupported nodes; raw rejection prevents automatic capacity claims for that target feature. ResizePolicy is already a1.27 field and retained.
findings.validationOrRequiredAction: Existing raw workload/HPA baseline tests cover mechanism; ensure representative unknown paths remain rejected after SDK upgrade.

findings.change: gitRepo default disabled, Portworx CSI GA, reclaim policy always honored, mutable CSI count alpha
findings.assessment: gitRepo is conservatively blocked including admission-added/old saved plans; CephFS/RBD guard carries forward. Transparently migrated Portworx is not blanket rejected but requires driver/security configuration. Converter does not create/delete/resize production PVC/PV, so reclaim/resize API changes do not alter its writes; fixture cleanup must respect owner UIDs/reclaim policy. CSINode attach limits and mounting remain declared limitations.
findings.validationOrRequiredAction: Retain legacy storage refusal/recovery tests; test regular CSI data continuity without claiming attachment-limit proof.

findings.change: ResourceQuota scope-update bug fix and new VolumeAttributesClass PVC quota scope
findings.assessment: Known supported Pod quota scopes are evaluated and unknown scope/operators fail for manual review. Source/target controller and actual Pod dryruns remain authoritative. The converter does not resize production PVCs/change VolumeAttributesClass. New unrelated PVC-only scope can conservatively refuse automatic preflight; do not claim unsupported scope is simulated.
findings.validationOrRequiredAction: Keep namespace/shared quota,full replica demand and unsupported-scope tests. Preflight does not reserve quota against concurrent changes.

findings.change: corev1 Endpoints deprecated but explicitly fully supported; terminatingReplicas status added
findings.assessment: Retained corev1 Endpoints reads continue valid. Added controller status fields do not require rejecting objects whose specs are baseline-compatible, and retirement checks use owned actual Pods rather than relying on new terminatingReplicas alone. EndpointSlice migration is maintenance; large truncated endpoint sets and external traffic remain qualified limits.
findings.validationOrRequiredAction: Keep real Service endpoint UID/HTTP/termination evidence and avoid claiming any deprecated API removal in1.33.

findings.change: Node-audience/azureFile fix, token binding stable, new namespace NetworkPolicies, image signature support
findings.assessment: Tokens remain opaque and projected audience settings preserved. Exact API failures are not bypassed by reviews. New system/operator NetworkPolicies are inventoried when relevant but policy selectors are not a complete traffic simulator; external CNI/registry/signature availability must be verified. Mirror tooling/console HPA form/OLM/platform changes do not change converter request bodies.
findings.validationOrRequiredAction: Maintain credential-expiry and image-trigger qualification; image/signature and storage-token behavior remain cluster prerequisites.

findings.change: SCC readonly-root/default and nested-container UID-range patch fixes
findings.assessment: Relevant patch notes change actual defaults/UID constraints. The converter reads current defaulted Pod semantics through actual SA review and server Pod admission and checks requiredSCC separately. It does not assume a fixed SCC priority/name/default across minors, overwrite SCCs or silently remove readOnlyRootFilesystem.
findings.validationOrRequiredAction: Keep SCC baseline-default/pinned authorization contracts. Distinguish these object-specific fixes from a blanket claim that all SCCs changed defaults.

historicalSnapshots: Exact snapshots and source-bound resolution overlays require the external evidence bundle.
